content.text:
Yes—this is practical, and the existing CI is already close to supporting it. Stellar/Perlmutter CI builds both the candidate and baseline, records candidate/baseline C-regression compilation times, and obtains Slurm allocation elapsed time (which excludes queue wait). It does not yet record candidate-versus-baseline execution time separately, so that would be the key addition.

I would not initially reject a PR based on “whole Jenkins wall-clock time.” It mixes Git checkout, dependency builds, cache state, login-node contention, and Slurm queueing. Instead, gate on explicitly timed, comparable workloads:

- candidate vs. baseline C-regression execution;
- candidate vs. baseline parallel C-regression execution;
- optionally, candidate vs. baseline unit-test execution;
- keep compilation/build timings as reporting signals, rather than part of the first gate.

A robust rule is both relative and absolute, e.g. fail only if the candidate is over 50% slower and exceeds the baseline by at least 5–10 minutes. This avoids rejecting a change from 2 s to 4 s while still catching a test suite that grows from 20 to 45 minutes. Measure the same workload with the same Slurm allocation and resource count, ideally repeat suspicious comparisons and use a median before blocking.

Pros:

- Prevents accidental expensive regressions or huge new tests from silently degrading CI.
- Makes runtime cost visible during review, where it is easiest to address.
- The baseline is the PR’s actual base revision, so it naturally evolves with `main`.
- Slurm’s recorded elapsed time avoids queue-delay noise.

Cons and pitfalls:

- Timing is noisy: shared hardware, filesystem load, GPU variability, frequency scaling, and cold caches can cause false failures.
- Candidate and baseline test inventories differ; a legitimate new high-value test will look like a regression.
- The current C-regression work is asymmetric: baseline creates reference outputs, candidate checks them. Those must be timed separately, and a candidate’s expanded suite may correctly cost more.
- A strict gate can incentivize under-testing or test splitting to evade the metric.
- Build timing is especially noisy and may punish legitimate compiler/configuration changes rather than test growth.
- CI currently omits the parallel regression Slurm elapsed time from `ci-timing-summary.txt`; that should be added before using it as a performance signal.

My preferred policy: start with a non-blocking GitHub status/comment for several weeks, collect distributions by pipeline, then enforce a hybrid threshold on test-execution allocation time only. Provide a reviewed opt-out label or CI parameter for justified expensive additions, with the measured delta displayed in the PR status.

Ok, I'll step back from making this a requirement. I think I just want to make sure that Jenkins records the time spent on "make install" (compilation) and on "runregression run create" vs "runregression run check", and store that somewhere that's easy to access, maybe as an artifact, or a feature in the existing databases. Similarly for clusters, I want to make sure we record time spent on compilation and actually running the tests (not building dependencies or waiting in the queue). What do you think?

That’s a better fit for the current CI: preserve timing as observability rather than a correctness gate. The existing summary already captures C-regression compile time and total Slurm allocation time, but it does not distinguish `create` from `check`, does not time `make install`, and omits parallel-regression elapsed time.

Yes. `ci-timing-summary.txt` is already written during each Stellar and Perlmutter build’s `finally` block, printed into the Jenkins console log, and archived as a Jenkins build artifact. You can access it from that build’s **Artifacts** page; it is not committed to the repository or stored in the regression SQLite databases. Its current contents are roughly:

```text
candidate_c_compile_seconds=…
baseline_c_compile_seconds=…
login_c_compile_seconds=…
unit_slurm_elapsed_seconds=…
regression_slurm_elapsed_seconds=…
```

So an artifact is the natural first home. It’s simple, durable per build, and has no schema migration or risk of confusing performance telemetry with numerical-regression results.

I’d extend it with command-level timings, rather than relying on the existing Slurm allocation elapsed time:

```text
candidate_install_seconds=…
baseline_install_seconds=…
candidate_c_regression_compile_seconds=…
baseline_c_regression_compile_seconds=…
unit_test_run_seconds=…
c_regression_create_seconds=…
c_regression_check_seconds=…
parallel_c_regression_create_seconds=…
parallel_c_regression_check_seconds=…
```

Each measurement would wrap only the relevant command (`make install`, `make unit-run`, or an individual `runregression … create/check`) with a monotonic elapsed-time measurement. That cleanly excludes dependency setup and Slurm queue delay. The existing Slurm elapsed fields can remain as useful allocation-level context, but should not be mistaken for exact test-runtime measurements.

One small current gap: parallel C-regression jobs are submitted, but their allocation elapsed time is not included in the summary; adding its command-level `create` and `check` metrics fixes that directly. The same structure can be used for both Stellar CPU and Perlmutter GPU.
I don't understand this gap you are referring to. Can you explain it in more detail?

The “gap” is only in the consolidated artifact, not in whether the parallel tests run.

Stellar CI runs three Slurm jobs:

| Job | Status file written | Included in `ci-timing-summary.txt`? |
|---|---|---|
| Unit tests | `slurm-unit-job-status.txt` | Yes |
| Ordinary C regressions | `slurm-regression-job-status.txt` | Yes |
| Parallel C regressions | `slurm-parallel-regression-job-status.txt` | No |

Every submitted Slurm job writes an `elapsed_seconds` value from Slurm accounting, so the parallel job’s elapsed time exists in its own archived status file. But `writeCiTimingSummary()` currently reads only the first two files and therefore does not copy the parallel elapsed time into `ci-timing-summary.txt`.

Also, the existing ordinary regression duration is a single allocation-level number. It covers both:

1. Baseline `runregression run … create`
2. Candidate `runregression run … check`

It cannot tell how much time each half consumed. The analogous parallel job has the same issue. The proposed command-level metrics would make those two phases individually visible.

Ok, good, we need these two phases to be individually timed, and included in ci-timing-summary.txt.

Ok, plese proceed with this expansion of ci-timing-summary.txt. I only ask that we also plan to do this for the personal and team machines.

I’ll treat this as a shared CI telemetry change: add separate `create` and `check` timings (including parallel C regressions) to the existing cluster summary, and introduce the same summary artifact for the personal/team pipeline, which the team Jenkinsfile delegates to.

<proposed_plan>
# CI timing-summary expansion

## Summary

Extend `ci-timing-summary.txt` into the common per-build timing artifact for Stellar CPU, Perlmutter GPU, personal CI, and team-workstation CI. Team workstation will receive the behavior through its existing delegation to the personal pipeline.

## Key changes

- Add timed `make install` phases for both candidate and baseline builds:
  `candidate_install_seconds` and `baseline_install_seconds`.
- Preserve existing C-regression compile metrics and add explicit runtime metrics for:
  `baseline_c_regression_create_seconds`,
  `candidate_c_regression_check_seconds`,
  `baseline_parallel_c_regression_create_seconds`, and
  `candidate_parallel_c_regression_check_seconds`.
- On Stellar and Perlmutter, record the elapsed time around each exact command inside the Slurm payload scripts, excluding Slurm queue wait and setup outside that command.
- Add the parallel Slurm allocation elapsed value to the cluster summaries for completeness, while retaining existing unit and ordinary-regression allocation metrics.
- Introduce the same summary-generation helper and artifact archival in `jenkinsfile.personal`; its values use the identical keys. The team workstation inherits it unchanged because it loads that pipeline.
- Continue printing the summary to the Jenkins console and archive `ci-timing-summary.txt` on successful, failed, or aborted builds. Missing phases retain the existing `not-recorded` convention.

## Test plan

- Validate Pipeline syntax/structure and shell syntax for all edited Jenkinsfiles and Slurm scripts.
- Confirm each summary contains the new keys after a representative local/personal run.
- Confirm Stellar and Perlmutter artifact summaries contain separate baseline `create` and candidate `check` values for both ordinary and parallel regressions, plus all Slurm allocation metrics.
- Confirm team-workstation builds archive the same personal-pipeline summary.

## Assumptions

- “Compilation” here includes `make install` and the already-recorded C-regression compilation timings; dependency-build timing remains intentionally excluded.
- “Test runtime” means wall time spent executing the individual `runregression … create` or `… check` command. It is telemetry only and does not affect CI pass/fail status.
</proposed_plan>

Not as precisely as the previous plan stated—the personal pipeline’s `make check` combines unit-test compilation and execution, so timing that command alone would not isolate test runtime.

The right adjustment is to split it into its existing equivalent commands:

```sh
make -j${jobs} unit
make unit-run
```

That makes the test-only runtime explicit, without changing what is tested. The baseline `create` and candidate `check` commands are already separate invocations, so each can be timed directly.

<proposed_plan>
# Granular Jenkins CI timing artifacts

## Summary

Extend `ci-timing-summary.txt` for all CI variants. It will record compilation/build and test-execution phases separately, while excluding dependency setup and Slurm queue wait. Team-workstation inherits the personal-pipeline implementation it already loads.

## Key changes

- In personal CI, replace `make -j… check` with sequential `make -j… unit` and `make unit-run`; time candidate and baseline unit-test builds and test-only execution separately.
- Time candidate and baseline `make install`, regression-test compilation, baseline ordinary/parallel `runregression … create`, and candidate ordinary/parallel `runregression … check`.
- Add matching command-level timings to Stellar CPU and Perlmutter GPU Slurm payloads. Their unit-test payload already uses `make unit-run`, so its measurement is test-only.
- Include all metrics in `ci-timing-summary.txt`, including ordinary and parallel Slurm allocation elapsed values as supplementary context. Keep `not-recorded` for a phase that does not start or complete.
- Generate, print, and archive the summary in the personal pipeline; team-workstation receives the identical artifact through `jenkinsfile.personal`.

## Summary keys

- `candidate_unit_build_seconds`, `baseline_unit_build_seconds`
- `candidate_unit_test_seconds`, `baseline_unit_test_seconds`
- `candidate_regression_build_seconds`, `baseline_regression_build_seconds`
- `candidate_install_seconds`, `baseline_install_seconds`
- `candidate_c_compile_seconds`, `baseline_c_compile_seconds`
- `candidate_parallel_c_compile_seconds`, `baseline_parallel_c_compile_seconds`
- `baseline_c_regression_create_seconds`, `candidate_c_regression_check_seconds`
- `baseline_parallel_c_regression_create_seconds`, `candidate_parallel_c_regression_check_seconds`
- Cluster-only allocation context: unit, ordinary-regression, and parallel-regression Slurm elapsed seconds.

## Test plan

- Validate Jenkins Pipeline and shell syntax for personal/team, Stellar, and Perlmutter paths.
- Run representative candidate/baseline builds and confirm that each `ci-timing-summary.txt` artifact contains separate unit-test, create, and check timings.
- Confirm personal and team builds preserve their existing tested commands and failure behavior after splitting `make check`.
- Confirm cluster command-level timing excludes Slurm queue time and parallel allocation timing appears in the summary.

## Assumptions

- Timings are informational artifacts only; no pass/fail threshold is introduced.
- “Unit-test runtime” means `make unit-run` only; unit compilation is reported separately.
</proposed_plan>

content.text:
Implemented CI timing telemetry across personal/team, Stellar CPU, and Perlmutter GPU.

Highlights:

- Personal/team now splits `make check` into `make unit` and `make unit-run`, recording candidate and baseline unit build/test durations separately.
- All pipelines record candidate/baseline `make install` time.
- Ordinary and parallel regression `create` and `check` commands are individually timed.
- Cluster summaries now include parallel-regression Slurm allocation elapsed time.
- Personal CI now writes and archives `ci-timing-summary.txt`; team-workstation inherits this via its shared pipeline.

Modified files include [jenkinsfile.personal](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/jenkinsfile.personal), [Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.stellar_cpu), and [Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu).

Validated with `bash -n` on all edited Slurm payloads and `git diff --check`. I did not run a Jenkins/Slurm build locally; no Groovy/Jenkins parser is installed in this environment.
So what stages will I see in the Jenkins UI Pipeline Overview now?

The Pipeline Overview stage names stay unchanged. The new timings are recorded inside those stages and shown in the archived `ci-timing-summary.txt`, not as new Jenkins UI stages.

For personal/team, you will still see:

- Resolve candidate and baseline
- Checkout candidate
- Report pending
- Build candidate
- Build baseline
- C regressions
- Parallel C regressions

For example, `Build candidate` still visually combines unit build, unit execution, regression build, and install—while the artifact separates their durations.

On Stellar/Perlmutter, the existing distinct stages remain, including:

- Build unit tests
- Run unit tests (SLURM)
- Install candidate for C regression
- Run C regressions (SLURM)
- Run parallel C regressions (SLURM)

If you want the Pipeline Overview itself to expose separate “Run candidate unit tests,” “Create baseline regressions,” and “Check candidate regressions” stages, that would be a separate UI-oriented refactor.
Can you make a plan for that UI-oriented refactor?

I’ll ground this in the current stage layout first. The key design choice is whether the UI should expose only execution phases (`unit-run`, `create`, `check`) or every measured compilation/build phase as well.

questions.question: How much of the timing breakdown should become visible Jenkins stages across personal/team and both cluster pipelines?

options.label: Execution phases only (Recommended)
options.description: Add separate unit-test, baseline-create, and candidate-check stages; retain existing build/compile stages.

options.label: Every measured phase
options.description: Expose unit/regression compilation and each install as separate stages too, for maximum detail but a long overview.

options.label: Personal only
options.description: Split only the coarse personal/team stages; leave cluster stage names unchanged.

content.text: For the cluster pipelines, distinct Jenkins `Create baseline` and `Check candidate` stages cannot simply wrap the current single Slurm job: it performs both commands in one allocation. Making them separate visible stages requires two Slurm jobs, which adds a second queue/allocation cycle.

questions.question: Which tradeoff should the plan adopt for cluster regression UI stages?

options.label: Split into two jobs (Recommended)
options.description: Show accurate create/check stages and independent timings, at the cost of another Slurm allocation and possible queue wait.

options.label: Keep one Slurm job
options.description: Avoid extra scheduler overhead; retain one combined regression stage while artifacts show split command times.

options.label: Separate only personal/team
options.description: Expose create/check UI stages locally, while cluster execution and overview remain unchanged.
